how: Members call participants to particular local works and upkeep tasks without demonstrating a numerical participation threshold.
Participants ask about the canvas and its labels and receive explanations of placement rules, names and alleged external threats.
A familiar local graffiti-wall analogy explains what the shared digital surface is without demonstrating recruitment.
Explanation remains necessary after pictures are already visible because some participants still do not know the rules or names.
A busy canvas and limited shared space do not establish a judgment that local hands or space cannot sustain the desired work.
A mistaken placement and departure for bed do not establish withdrawal under strain or repair of an interpersonal quarrel.
The skyline proposal establishes a starter act independently of the separate member who answers it.
A member answers the skyline proposal with a bare report for duty.
The skyline proposal receives a bare acceptance without showing how every reader responds.
The skyline proposal draws commitment and pixel reports, supporting a local proposal-response sequence rather than a measured recruitment effect.
The original logo is already visible, and the skyline proposal does not reveal a distinct starter-to-recruitment mechanism.
Members propose local lettering and a skyline, display a national contribution and include the Arch in shared work.
Members report placed pixels, correction of their own errors and the current state of local work.
A link request receives canvas coordinates, establishing minimal location sharing without an official pixel template.
Coordinates and design proposals occur without a coded exchange showing design argument settled by a pixel template.
Construction includes identifying and correcting one's own misplaced pixels before the complete picture is finished.
The building-to-keeping order applies to placed parts rather than requiring completion of the whole picture before repair begins.
Praise and labour reports around an already-visible logo do not establish that a completion report caused celebration.
A helper leaves for bed while the work's overnight survival remains uncertain.
A participant reports fitting canvas help into paid working time.
Available upkeep depends on personal time as a helper leaves to sleep while hoping the work survives overnight.
Platform limits bound action through the placement timer and shutdown even when a participant remains willing to help.
An allegation about external bots does not establish local adoption of scripts or spare accounts.
Defence and alleged external automation are reported without evidence that upkeep pressure caused local automation adoption.
Reported orders from overlapping groups prevent treating local coordination as demonstrably commandless while their authority and enforcement remain unresolved.
A single room cannot test the global frequency claim, and reported orders do not expose its complete decision structure.
A relayed message and a named outside fan group do not establish moving local planning into a chat.
Messages relaying an agreement and accusations about rivals do not establish local secrecy or infiltration.
Members restore changed pixels, clean logos, seek protection and recount standing watch.
Members identify their own placement errors and exchange accusations and denials about changes to the work.
An admission of colouring the neighbouring hat is followed by an observation that somebody repaired it, without identifying the repairer.
Informed opposition must be distinguished from uninformed restoration because a builder rejects a ceasefire immediately after hearing about it.
Communicating the agreed form cannot alone ensure compatible upkeep where informed placers also need reasons to accept restraint.
Participants report and contest an agreement over the hat and a ceasefire over overlapping work.
Agreements circulate through messages, reported orders and crossposts before participants try to secure compliance in the host room.
Visitors carry a neighbouring group's warning and conditional help offer or explain an agreement without establishing formal delegation.
Members invoke prior claims, preserve neighbouring pictures and try to rein in local attackers.
Participants report reciprocal upkeep and thank helpers across groups.
Mutual upkeep and an explicit alliance instantiate minimal coalition work without revealing a coordinating council.
Reported upkeep and agreements do not reveal whether erosion caused the first border negotiation.
Reciprocal help is reported without a shortage-of-hands passage linking upkeep strain to requesting that help.
An alliance and mutual maintenance are visible without evidence that maintenance pressure caused coalition formation.
The reported bargain explicitly makes tolerating the neighbour the condition for receiving maintenance help.
Invoking an agreement supplies a reason to leave the neighbouring wizard in place.
Restraint needs repeated compliance work because later placers can still assert priority or pursue expansion.
Members argue for preserving others' work by preferring positive creation over cancellation and rejecting protection through overwriting.
A challenge to an agreement and efforts to stop vandalism do not explicitly state who may bind the room.
Agreement followed by refusal does not establish an authority dispute when the refusal opposes terms without questioning who may represent the room.
The skyline proposal chooses a spot beside existing work without requiring a prior recorded loss.
A reported small shift can preserve an existing contribution without demonstrating the loss-driven migration described elsewhere in the model.
A conditional relocation offer, a small preserved shift and a post-close restart request do not establish loss-driven migration.
Shared overlap and an offer of relocation help do not establish a host ruling over dependent guest work.
Helping another group and admitting school-affiliated sabotage do not establish dual belonging or being torn between two rooms.
Members bring local and national identities into lettering, contributions and sports slogans.
Sports and school affiliations identify canvas antagonists while a retrospective accusation invokes older rivalry conduct.
Named rival affiliations appear in the turns describing defacement and sabotage without making those acts unanimous room policy.
A caller jokes about feeling like a rival fan after learning the hat attack breaches an agreement.
A joke responding to unrelated platform automation does not become a joke made from canvas work merely by appearing under a canvas post.
Naming an outside fan group, crossposting and opening a megathread do not establish formation of a new canvas room.
A vandalized slogan and its explanation do not establish an argument about offensive language or refusal of hate symbols.
A megathread title establishes an attempt to gather canvas talk as placement ends.
Opening a container cannot establish effective routing, moderator enforcement or live coordination when placement ends immediately afterward.
Effective containment requires time to gather ongoing work, whereas a megathread opened at shutdown demonstrates only an attempted container.
The late thread does not reveal whether a flood of recruitment calls caused its opening.
Placement instructions and a megathread do not establish a host takeover or prank that made canvas calls ambiguous.
Criticizing the megathread's timing does not establish attacking the room's own mark because of unwanted canvas posts.
Members praise visible marks and celebrate their scale, survival and completion before and after closure.
Participants record survival, loss and finality through statements accompanying the visible work.
Celebrating and recording survival can coincide in one finality statement rather than requiring distinct successive acts.
A wish for lasting friendship instantiates prospective continuation without demonstrating an enduring organization.
A friendship wish answers a final-canvas post without establishing that recording caused the wish.
Visitors' congratulations and partnership reports do not explicitly establish that the canvas brought newcomers or lapsed members into the room.
Praising a team-related mark does not establish seeking notice from the team, creators or press outside the canvas.
Closure includes a willing participant learning that placement has ended after offering to restart the work.
A post-close participant learns that the canvas has ended and expresses disappointment.
The specific restart exchange is resolved by learning that placement ended rather than by judging capacity and choosing a new spot.
Finality and survival claims do not show a contest over cleanup or which version of the event should be preserved.
Members rally against the hat, report defacement, admit sabotage and insist on expansion despite a ceasefire.
Attack calls receive explicit reasons for restraint and, in two exchanges, regret or acceptance from the caller.
An attack rally prompts invocation of an existing agreement rather than a newly observed negotiation.
Participants answer a neighbour defiantly and carry sports conflict through accusations about another group's destructive conduct.
A rival-logo removal call develops through a restraint reply into accusations about a rival group.
Recruitment and attacks coexist without evidence that recruitment caused those particular attackers to arrive.

statement: Answering platform automation with an unrelated community teaching
how: A human corrects a battery bot and invokes charge-your-phone teachings as a side joke without a demonstrated role in organizing pixel work.
